source: Javanmardi et al. PHME 2024, https://github.com/alireza-javanmardi/bearing-RUL/tree/d7167c927aad5b7f197b1d735b21339e3e17844e. U. Paderborn single rig, Zenodo 10868257. Previous examination of B01/B17 only checked waveform compatibility; the authors' documentation and file counts have been inspected before design, no prediction has been scored on this apparatus. Use author-extracted 200 spectral amplitudes, observed settings and acquisition timestamps. No official vertical sensor, no imputation of that channel. Compare a maintenance policy with a shared site adapter; do not assign this a score for the competition neural weights.
eligibility: Only runs with a recorded stopping threshold in the original documentation table 3. Exclude B01 and interrupted B05, and B16 without a named stopping threshold. Order by actual first timestamp, use first four completed eligible runs as initial archive. Score every 20th row beginning with row 0 on every remaining run, not an end-dependent selection. End = last operating timestamp. Inspect timestamp monotonicity, duplicate/time gaps, alignment; fail closed on unexplained FFT / operating timestamp counts, allow author-documented trailing operating-only rows, use last physical operating observation as end in that case. Multiple sessions / downward jumps require original timing verification, never reorder the vibration stream. If service starts before fourth archive is completed, disclose and score only after availability. No target duration or future vibration vector for predicting a row; do not pass a unit ID as a numerical feature. Training consumes completed, nonoverlapping units only. Deadline for incorporating reference labels is strictly before the start of the service bearing; decisions frozen for that bearing, account separately for overlaps. This is leave-forward real calendar evaluation; every tested device may later become a reference once its experiment finishes.
metrics: Primary remaining calendar minutes to actual last observation, pooled RMSE and equal-bearing mean RMSE, plus maximum per-bearing RMSE, MAE, counts, timings. Large acquisition gaps (more than 5 median within-unit cadence) are audited; repeat scoring with active clock capped at twice each unit's FIRST positive cadence (available by second row; accrued intervals only). Cadence baseline for first row uses 12 s. This sensitivity-only target changes training and scoring clocks together. Count earliest eligible returns and changed predictions.
candidates: Same raw readings, target and prior complete labels; fixed installation archive vs always replace with all completed runs before each new bearing. Installed methods: empirical conditional remaining-life mean from past total lifetimes exceeding current attained age; if all shorter, use mean historical lifespan as exponential tail residual. Also median countdown clipped at 0. PHME-derived fixed method: same twenty adjacent max spectral pools + six current operating fields + training-only minmax scaling + sklearn HistGradientBoostingRegressor defaults, random_state 2000. For minutes train on absolute remaining minutes over all phases, no retrospective transition annotation or division by service lifespan. Include spectral-only HGBoost and operating+vibration+observed age HGBoost separately; clip negative minutes to zero. Train every 20th row equally as scored. Raw author main.py with op_feature, B17, bucket20 seed0, official transition mapping and all other 16 source runs will separately reproduce the authors' own normalized degradation-only MAE; different target AND information from forward minute scores. No retrospective target labels enter forward policy.
decision: Cold incumbent is cumulative PHME-feature regressor for every strategy that chooses. For each arriving independent bearing save its actual predictions from all fixed candidate families with cumulative refit. After failure archive each candidate's device-level MSE for that bearing. An ongoing policy picks smallest mean of past released MSE, with at least 1 percent MSE gain over incumbent required, tie retains old. Once waits for first scored-and-failed device then fixes method. Nearest historical operating condition variant selects using the three nearest prior scored-and-failed devices to the FIRST currently measured load/speed vector (training-only source feature std, squared standardized distance; use all if fewer than three). No current target label, no future test operating states, no selection of hypothesis after scoring. Strong fixed controls include the above methods both archive-frozen and always-refit. Evaluation sees all tools; report actual cost of shared-fit comparison and counts; do not impute single-policy cost. Hindsight chooses best arm per device as a headroom diagnostic only. Operational match to published method does not imply access to entire test life at prediction.
old_policy: Also run the unchanged project HistoricalToolChoice (device-equal, no switching margin) against the very same candidate tools and the common initial PHME-feature model. Include a separately scored previously installed project phase-tree recipe: reuse its fixed CatBoost estimator settings, train on source remaining fraction, rescale by median completed device lifespan, using the same 20 pooled spectral features here. Fixed original model tensor interface cannot read these horizontal channels. Do not add the retrospective phase-tree control to the frozen chooser menu.
adoption: At least 2 percent pooled RMSE improvement over strongest fixed control and over informed once; worst-device RMSE no more than 1 percent worse than strongest fixed. Inspect per-device wins and equal-device score, report negative outcome. If no such gain, reject selector as default and inspect what the best frozen model gets wrong before adding more selectors. If large error resides before feedback or all candidate estimates share a failure mode, change training/reference. Record all arms, feedback windows and per-row delivered values. Verify on existing XJTU and PRONOSTIA with actual failure labels where appropriate before any product default.
